channel.title: Omarchy Stories
channel.description:
Omarchy Stories — A signal from nowhere.

This is a transmission by the community, for the community.

Omarchy is beautiful, fun & agentic Linux — opinionated by DHH, but yours to command. And behind every install there's a story: the developer who stopped renting their workflow from Cupertino, the tinkerer who vibed their way through an alteration nobody thought possible, the stubborn fix that became community knowledge overnight.

Omarchy Stories broadcasts those people. Each episode is a field report from someone in command — what they escaped, what they changed, what they fixed, and what the next Omarch can learn from it.

No gatekeepers, no marketing filter, no permission required.

If you have an interesting Omarchy story, this is your platform.

Because that's the whole point: when something breaks, nobody here waits for Apple or Microsoft to allow the fix.

Someone finds it. Someone shares it. Everybody moves faster.

The community is the signal. Tune in.

We can fix everything.

item.title: 009 Joel Gaff, Jr. - AI Coding: Are We Shipping Faster and Learning Less?
item.description:
AI can help you ship faster. But are you still learning to build software you understand and can maintain?

In Omarchy Stories 009, Basti sits down with Joel Gaff Jr., a Ruby on Rails developer, former Ironman race director, and creator of Rails Guild and Omarchy Guild. They explore the trade-offs between AI-assisted coding and learning by doing, the hidden costs of maintaining AI-built apps, and what happens to small SaaS businesses when software becomes easier to copy.

Beyond the code, they talk about the people behind Rails and Omarchy, building tools for yourself, and finding the confidence to share your work. From a train crossing an Ironman bike course to publishing before you feel ready, this is a conversation about learning, adapting, and getting things out into the world.

IN THIS EPISODE

• Learning Rails hands-on while AI changes how software is built
• Shipping faster without losing understanding of your code
• AI-generated software, maintenance, token costs, and small SaaS products
• Omarchy, Linux devices, and agents that automate everyday workflows
• Rails Guild, Omarchy Guild, and the value of welcoming communities
• Imposter syndrome, building in public, and choosing done over perfect

item.title: 008 Alexander Zeitler - Running a Manufacturing Company on Omarchy & AI Agents
item.description:
What happens when a manufacturing company stops accepting vendor lock-in and rebuilds its workflow around open tools, AI agents, and event sourcing?

Basti talks with Alexander Zeitler, a software veteran who runs a 10-person manufacturing business on Linux and Omarchy. After discovering he couldn't access his own data in a legacy ERP, he used Claude to extract it and started replacing siloed workflows with a system he actually controls.

In this episode:
• Why "owning" your data means nothing if you can't use it
• FreeCAD, OpenSCAD, Python and Rails in real manufacturing workflows
• Building products from parameters, not proprietary CAD
• Generating decision records, risk assessments and docs from reusable blocks
• GitHub issues as event streams, with agents that reason before they code
• A second AI review layer for every code change
• Why event sourcing matters more in an AI-assisted world
